newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: GOLF-LEANEY HOLDS ON TO WIN VICTORIAN OPEN.
newsitem.headline: GOLF-LEANEY HOLDS ON TO WIN VICTORIAN OPEN.

text.p: Australian golfer Stephen Leaney held off a series of late challenges on Sunday to win his second successive Victorian Open title by one shot.
Leaney fired a final round of even-par 72 at the Victorian Golf Club to finish on eight-under-par 280, one shot clear of fellow Australians Darren Cole and Euan Walters.
Cole and Walters both carded final rounds of 71.

Leaney had led after each of the first three rounds but briefly surrendered the lead to Cole on Sunday after dropping three shots in four of his first eight holes. He regained his composure and the lead with birdies at the ninth and 15th holes.
Cole and Walters both missed birdie putts on the final hole which would have forced a play-off with Leaney.
"I was in front for about 60 holes and then lost the lead, but it didn't worry me," Leaney said.
"To have someone go in front actually settled me down."
Leaney set up his second Victorian title with a course record 64 in Thursday's first round, which he then followed with three consecutive level-par rounds.
Australians Peter Lonard and Geoff Ogilvy, an amateur, tied for fourth on 282, with European Tour regular Robert Allenby and Steve Allan another shot back on five-under.
New Zealand's Michael Long and Steve Alker were the best-placed overseas players, the pair finishing in a group of four players on 285.
